reason: The cited evidence (E1) only discusses stress-dependent creep mechanism transitions (diffusion vs. dislocation-dominated) in HEAs, without mentioning phase boundaries, their coherency, or their role in pinning dislocations. Therefore, none of the key premises about phase boundary effects are supported by the provided evidence.
premises: Coherent FCC/BCC phase boundaries act as effective obstacles to dislocation motion.
Increasing the density of coherent phase boundaries reduces dislocation mobility and plastic strain accumulation.
Reduced dislocation mobility leads to a lower steady-state creep rate.
Creep in FCC/BCC HEAs can be dislocation-dominated under certain conditions.
